title: The Macroeconomics Of AI: Part II
gist: Gavekal argues the macroeconomic payoff from AI hinges less on further gains in model capability than on the 'k' factor: how fast knowledge diffuses through the layers of the economy, which could keep lifting productivity even if AI progress plateaus.

themes.theme: The 'k' factor: knowledge diffusion as the real macro driver

insights.claim: The economic impact of AI will depend not on the technology's progress alone but on the interaction of three global factors, of which the most important is the 'k' factor: how rapidly knowledge diffuses across the different layers of the economy.
insights.speaker: Didier Darcet
insights.so_what: Investors tracking AI's macro impact should look past headline model-capability benchmarks and instead watch diffusion/adoption metrics across industries and firm layers as the real leading indicator of economic payoff.
insights.quote: The bigger macroeconomic question is the “k” factor, or how rapidly knowledge diffuses across the different layers of the economy.

insights.claim: Even if AI's information-processing capabilities eventually plateau, the pace of knowledge diffusion through the economy could still drive substantial gains in global productivity.
insights.speaker: Didier Darcet
insights.so_what: A capability plateau in frontier AI models would not necessarily cap the macro/productivity upside, so investors shouldn't equate slowing model breakthroughs with the end of the AI productivity story.
insights.quote: This factor could point to substantial gains in global productivity—even if information-processing capabilities eventually plateau.

insights.claim: As of this writing, there is no visible sign that AI's information-processing capability advances are slowing or plateauing.
insights.speaker: Didier Darcet
insights.so_what: With capability gains still accelerating and diffusion effects layered on top, the productivity tailwind case remains intact for now, arguing against near-term bets on an AI capex or capability slowdown.
insights.quote: And for now, there is little sign of any such plateau.
